rationale: The workflow already caches the Go build cache and Go dependencies in every Go-dependent job (check-diff, lint, unit-tests, e2e-tests, publish-artifacts), so the P-LIT-GHA-CACHE dependency-cache pattern's contraindication 'An equivalent cache already exists' applies. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT is not safely applicable: the measured evidence used a 5-minute job timeout, but CI history shows successful workflow runs taking 10-14 minutes, and jobs such as e2e-tests and publish-artifacts build Docker images, so a 5-minute limit risks violating the contraindication 'Valid slow runs exceed the proposed limit'. No other pattern fits: P-LIT-FAIL-FAST requires matrices (none present), P-LIT-CHANGE-FILTER risks missing required checks in a project with generated code and shared configuration, P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE conflicts with the publish/deployment job, and P-LIT-SKIP-WORKFLOW/P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE are ci_service-scoped rather than workflow edits.
